resources.string: Wake the screen by shaking your phone. Maracas looks for a few quick shakes in a row, and the sensitivity setting controls how much movement counts. Lower sensitivity helps avoid accidental wakes.
Wake when uncovered or flipped up

Uses the proximity sensor and the existing pickup/flip detection to wake the screen when the phone is moved out of a covered or face-down position. Availability and behavior depend on the device\'s sensors.
Skip shakes while the phone is covered
Uses the proximity sensor to suppress shake-triggered wakes while the phone appears to be covered or inside a pocket. Detection depends on the device\'s sensor behavior.
This device has no proximity sensor, so this option has no effect.
Shake sensitivity, left is a harder shake, right is a lighter shake

The slider moves the shake threshold between about 4.0 g at the left (low sensitivity, a hard shake is needed) and 1.8 g at the right (high sensitivity, a light shake is enough). 1 g is the pull of normal gravity. It only affects Shake to wake.

Maracas is on but its service is not running. Switch it off and on to restart.

This card shows what Maracas is doing, not how much power it uses. Android does not give apps a reliable measurement of their own battery use, so none is shown.

"Monitoring active" means Maracas's foreground service is running. It keeps listening to your phone's sensors while the screen is off and holds a CPU wake lock for that. A CPU wake lock keeps the processor awake, not the screen. Shake detection reads the accelerometer frequently, so it costs more than pickup detection.

"Battery usage" shows whether Android currently restricts Maracas in the background. For real consumption, see Settings > Battery.
Open Settings > Apps > Maracas > Battery and set Unrestricted
Allow Maracas to turn the screen off?

Android only lets an app lock the screen if you make it a device administrator.

Maracas asks for one permission only: locking the screen. It cannot erase data, change your password or see your files.

Tap Continue and Android will show its own activation screen. You stay in control: nothing is activated until you confirm there.

To remove it later, tap Remove here, or open Settings > Security > Device admin apps (the exact menu name varies by ROM), choose Maracas and deactivate it. Android will not let you uninstall Maracas while it is active.
Maracas needs this only to turn the screen off when you tap \"Turn screen off\". It requests no other administrator rights.
